summary: Intermittent stream stall after upstream multipath IP flap - final event never delivered to client
description: Issue summary: Customer reports repeated requests where an open websocket/SSE stream completes generation server-side but the client never receives the terminal/end event or final token. The connection closes from the edge with no terminal message and the client sees an 'incomplete' final choice. Impact: Several production customers on Dedicated have brief but recurring user-visible partial outputs in the last 1-3 tokens. This breaks downstream parsers and creates incorrect UI states (spinners that never finish). Frequency: ~1–3 occurrences per day across a subset of sessions using the customer's dedicated pool. Environment: Customer on Dedicated capacity in us-east behind our managed edge-proxy and a load-balancer that performs multipath routing for egress. Observed behavior: - Generation completes on serving-hosts (trace shows final EmitChoice/END record) - Edge/proxy closes TCP connection to client with FIN before END event is reliably delivered to client library - Client SDK receives truncated stream or EOF without terminal event; does not trigger resume because resume token is missing/never exposed - No obvious 5xx in upstream logs, edge shows connection close reason: RST (or half-close) in proxied path
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer workload (long chat generation ~400 tokens) on dedicated pool behind edge-proxy multipath routing
2) Run with intermittent simulated path swap (network flapping / multipath change) from test LB
3) Observe client receives stream but occasionally never gets terminal event despite backend EmitChoice logged
4) Reproduce more reliably by enabling short-lived path churn (curl or websocket test harness behind LB)
logs:
Selected traces and timestamps: 
- serving-host-07 (2026-03-01T14:02:12Z): emit_choice final="." id=gen-8f1f END-emitted=true trace=gen-8f1f
- edge-proxy-35 (2026-03-01T14:02:12Z): proxied-to-client FIN sent while upstream still streaming; upstream close observed 2026-03-01T14:02:12.120Z; client TCP FIN at 2026-03-01T14:02:12.115Z
- client-sdk (customer log) (2026-03-01T14:02:12Z): received EOF without end-event; last token index 399
Correlation: edge window shows a <100ms timing overlap where path swap triggered premature close. No 5xx on serving-hosts.
Relevant snapshot links: https://observability.redwood.ai/trace/gen-8f1f (internal)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Edge/load-balancer multipath switch triggers a TCP teardown on one path while backend continues to produce final tokens on another; the atomicity of our 'finalization' event is lost if the edge does not forward the last chunk before issuing FIN. Evidence: edge proxy logs show FIN close prior to final ACK from upstream in ~60% of samples for affected sessions. The serving runtime consistently logs END/Emit events. Additional hypothesis: client SDK's resume logic requires a terminal marker or a resume-token emitted in-stream; if the terminal marker is missing the SDK treats the session as a hard EOF and does not call 'resume' flow. Tests: repeated reproduce with synthetic path churn produced same symptom within 30 minutes. Edge team reproduced local harness when forcing half-close ordering. Related to previously observed edge keepalive/coalescing timing (see linked SUP-842117). Potential fixes: - ensure edge buffers and flushes terminal chunk before initiating close (drain window) - add idempotent terminal marker persisted to stream metadata so resume can detect missing terminal and request a replay - adjust SDK to attempt resume when last-seen sequence < final-expected and connection closed without end marker
temporary_workaround:
1) Customer can enable websocket sticky session to reduce multipath rebinds in LB configuration (recommended for now)
2) Increase keepalive window on edge-proxy to avoid immediate close during path swap
3) For critical clients, enable structured end-marker in request metadata (if available) so client can attempt resume on missing marker

root_cause: Premature connection teardown at the edge during multipath LB handoff that occasionally closed the client connection before the final terminal chunk was forwarded, combined with SDK resume logic that requires an explicit terminal marker to trigger a resume.
resolution: Work in progress: Edge team to deploy drain-and-flush change to staging (edge-proxy PR referenced). SDK team to add fallback resume attempt when connection closes without terminal marker (separate internal INT ticket planned). Customer workaround (sticky sessions) successfully reduced occurrences. Next steps: schedule coordinated rollout and test under path-flap harness; update runbook and add a regression test in our CI streaming harness.
